phrases.translation: Alif-Lãm-Ra. These are the verses of the Book; the clear Quran
phrases.explanation: The surah opens with the separated letters Alif-Lãm-Ra and identifies the verses as belonging to the clear Quran. The opening introduces a revelation presented as guidance that can be understood and followed.

phrases.translation: ˹The day will come when˺ the disbelievers will certainly wish they had submitted ˹to Allah˺
phrases.explanation: A day will come when disbelievers wish they had submitted to Allah. The verse contrasts their present rejection with the regret they will feel when the consequences are fully clear.

phrases.translation: ˹So˺ let them eat and enjoy themselves and be diverted by ˹false˺ hope, for they will soon know
phrases.explanation: The disbelievers are told to eat, enjoy themselves, and be distracted by false hope, because they will soon know the outcome. The warning exposes how short-term pleasure can conceal a serious future.

phrases.translation: We have never destroyed a society without a destined term
phrases.explanation: No society is destroyed before its appointed term. The verse places the timing of a community’s end within Allah’s decree rather than human impatience or prediction. for the society involved.

phrases.translation: No people can advance their doom, nor can they delay it
phrases.explanation: A people cannot bring their appointed doom forward or delay it. The warning answers those who either demand immediate punishment or assume it will never arrive. The appointed term is not subject to human bargaining.

phrases.translation: They say, “O you to whom the Reminder is revealed! You must be insane
phrases.explanation: The opponents mockingly call the Prophet insane because the Reminder has been revealed to him. Their insult avoids addressing the message and attacks the person delivering it. rather than engaging with his claims.

phrases.translation: Why do you not bring us the angels, if what you say is true?”
phrases.explanation: They demand that angels be brought if the Prophet is truthful. The request sets their preferred condition for belief instead of responding to the revelation already given. as a condition for accepting the message.

phrases.translation: We do not send the angels down except for a just cause, and then ˹the end of˺ the disbelievers will not be delayed
phrases.explanation: Angels descend only for a just cause, and then the disbelievers’ end is not delayed. Their demand ignores that an angelic visit may mark judgment rather than the reassurance they expect.

phrases.translation: It is certainly We Who have revealed the Reminder, and it is certainly We Who will preserve it
phrases.explanation: Allah says that He revealed the Reminder. The verse directly answers the mockery of the Prophet by identifying the source of the message as divine. Allah also promises to preserve the Reminder. The assurance places the Quran’s safeguarding in His care rather than in the opponents’ power to erase it.

phrases.translation: Indeed, We sent messengers before you ˹O Prophet˺ among the groups of early peoples
phrases.explanation: Messengers were sent before the Prophet among earlier peoples. The verse places his mission in a long history of guidance rather than treating it as an isolated event. This is part of a continuing pattern.

phrases.translation: but no messenger ever came to them without being mocked
phrases.explanation: Earlier messengers were mocked whenever they came to their people. The repeated pattern helps the Prophet understand that ridicule is not proof that a message is false. Ridicule is not a new response to truth.

phrases.translation: This is how We allow disbelief ˹to steep˺ into the hearts of the wicked
phrases.explanation: Disbelief is allowed to steep into the hearts of the wicked. The verse describes how continued rejection can become settled within a person rather than changing after each warning. over time.

phrases.translation: They would not believe in this ˹Quran˺ despite the ˹many˺ examples of those ˹destroyed˺ before
phrases.explanation: The people refuse to believe in the Quran despite examples of earlier communities who were destroyed. Their failure to learn from history shows that evidence alone does not help someone determined to reject it.

phrases.translation: And even if We opened for them a gate to heaven, through which they continued to ascend
phrases.explanation: Even if a gate to heaven were opened and the disbelievers ascended through it, the scene would not necessarily change their response. The verse challenges the idea that extraordinary sights alone can overcome a determined refusal to believe.

phrases.translation: still they would say, “Our eyes have truly been dazzled! In fact, we must have been bewitched.”
phrases.explanation: They would claim that their eyes were dazzled or that they had been bewitched. Their imagined response shows how they might explain away even a remarkable sign rather than accept its meaning.

phrases.translation: Indeed, We have placed constellations in the sky, and adorned it for all to see
phrases.explanation: Allah places constellations in the sky and adorns it for people to see. The heavens are presented as both ordered and beautiful, inviting people to look carefully at creation. for anyone who looks.

phrases.translation: And We protected it from every accursed devil
phrases.explanation: The sky is protected from every accursed devil. The verse describes a boundary that prevents devils from freely accessing what is beyond their reach. as a sign of divine protection.

phrases.translation: except the one eavesdropping, who is then pursued by a visible flare
phrases.explanation: An eavesdropper who tries to listen is pursued by a visible flare. The verse portrays attempted access as limited and resisted, underlining that the unseen is not open to devils at will.

phrases.translation: As for the earth, We spread it out and placed upon it firm mountains, and caused everything to grow there in perfect balance
phrases.explanation: Allah spreads out the earth and places firm mountains upon it. The land is prepared as a stable home for the creatures who live on it. Everything is caused to grow in perfect balance. The verse points to order and proportion in the living world rather than to unregulated growth.

phrases.translation: And We made in it means of sustenance for you and others, who you do not provide for
phrases.explanation: Allah provides means of sustenance for people and for creatures they do not provide for. The verse reminds humanity that provision extends far beyond what people themselves can produce or manage.

phrases.translation: There is not any means ˹of sustenance˺ whose reserves We do not hold, only bringing it forth in precise measure
phrases.explanation: Every means of sustenance has reserves held by Allah and is brought forth in precise measure. The verse presents provision as carefully apportioned, not as something that exists beyond His knowledge or control.

phrases.translation: We send fertilizing winds, and bring down rain from the sky for you to drink. It is not you who hold its reserves
phrases.explanation: Allah sends winds that help fertilize and brings down rain for people to drink. The verse reminds people that even the water they depend on comes from Him, not from stores they control.

phrases.translation: Surely it is We Who give life and cause death. And We are the ˹Eternal˺ Successor
phrases.explanation: Allah gives life and causes death, and He is the Eternal Successor. Human generations pass away, while Allah remains and holds authority over what follows. No created being can escape that cycle.

phrases.translation: We certainly know those who have gone before you and those who will come after ˹you˺
phrases.explanation: Allah knows those who came before and those who will come after. Every generation is within His knowledge, so no one is overlooked when the time for judgment arrives. This includes generations yet unborn.

phrases.translation: Surely your Lord ˹alone˺ will gather them together ˹for judgment˺. He is truly All-Wise, All-Knowing
phrases.explanation: Allah will gather everyone together for judgment. He is All-Wise and All-Knowing, so His decision accounts for every person and deed with complete understanding. His judgment is also perfectly just.

phrases.translation: Indeed, We created man from sounding clay moulded from black mud
phrases.explanation: Humanity is created from sounding clay moulded from black mud. The verse recalls the human origin described in revelation and humbles people who might otherwise become proud of their status.

phrases.translation: As for the jinn, We created them earlier from smokeless fire
phrases.explanation: The jinn are created earlier from smokeless fire. The verse distinguishes their origin from the human creation described immediately before, while both remain creations of Allah. Their different origins do not change their dependence on Him.

phrases.translation: ˹Remember, O Prophet˺ when your Lord said to the angels, “I am going to create a human being from sounding clay moulded from black mud
phrases.explanation: Allah tells the angels that He will create a human being from sounding clay. The announcement prepares for the command that follows and marks the human creation as significant in the story.

phrases.translation: So when I have fashioned him and had a spirit of My Own ˹creation˺ breathed into him, fall down in prostration to him.”
phrases.explanation: After fashioning the human and breathing into him a spirit of His creation, Allah commands the angels to prostrate. The verse presents this as an act of obedience to Allah’s command and honor for the human being.

phrases.translation: So the angels prostrated all together—
phrases.explanation: All the angels prostrate together in response to Allah’s command. Their collective obedience contrasts with the refusal of Iblis described in the next verse. Their response is an example of immediate obedience.

phrases.translation: but not Iblîs, who refused to prostrate with the others
phrases.explanation: Iblis refuses to prostrate with the angels. His exception marks the beginning of open disobedience in the account and sets up the question about his reason. He places his own judgment above the command he received.

phrases.translation: Allah asked, “O Iblîs! What is the matter with you that you did not join others in prostration?”
phrases.explanation: Allah asks Iblis why he did not join the others in prostration. The question confronts his refusal directly and gives him an opportunity to explain himself. The account presents his refusal as deliberate.

phrases.translation: He replied, “It is not for me to prostrate to a human You created from sounding clay moulded from black mud.”
phrases.explanation: Iblis refuses because he considers himself above a human created from clay. His answer reveals pride and contempt for Allah’s command, rather than a lack of understanding. His answer exposes the pride behind his disobedience.

phrases.translation: Allah commanded, “Then get out of Paradise, for you are truly cursed
phrases.explanation: Allah orders Iblis to leave Paradise and declares him cursed. The command is the consequence of his refusal to obey and his prideful response. He has no right to resist his Creator.

phrases.translation: And surely upon you is condemnation until the Day of Judgment.”
phrases.explanation: Iblis is condemned until the Day of Judgment. The lasting condemnation shows the seriousness of his defiance and the separation it creates from divine favor. The judgment follows his choice to defy Allah.

phrases.translation: Satan appealed, “My Lord! Then delay my end until the Day of their resurrection.”
phrases.explanation: Iblis asks Allah to delay his end until the Day of resurrection. His request seeks time to continue acting against humanity rather than expressing repentance for his refusal. The delay does not undo the wrongdoing he has committed.

phrases.translation: Allah said, “You will be delayed
phrases.explanation: Allah grants Iblis a delay. The permission is limited by the appointed term that follows and does not mean his rebellion has been approved. Granting time is not an endorsement of his aims.

phrases.translation: until the appointed Day.”
phrases.explanation: The delay lasts only until the appointed Day. The fixed limit shows that Iblis’s activity is not endless and remains subject to Allah’s decision. His period of influence therefore has a boundary.

phrases.translation: Satan responded, “My Lord! For allowing me to stray I will surely tempt them on earth and mislead them all together
phrases.explanation: Iblis says he will tempt people on earth and mislead them because he blames Allah for allowing him to stray. His speech reveals defiance and an intention to draw people into wrongdoing.

phrases.translation: except Your chosen servants among them.”
phrases.explanation: Iblis acknowledges that Allah’s chosen servants are an exception to his plan. The verse confirms that his influence is not absolute and that sincere servants remain under Allah’s protection. His influence does not remove their ability to choose.

phrases.translation: Allah said, “This is the Way, binding on Me
phrases.explanation: Allah declares that this is the Way, binding upon Him. The statement answers Satan’s intention to mislead people by affirming that Allah’s straight path and promise remain established. Satan’s plan remains bounded by Allah’s authority.

phrases.translation: you will certainly have no authority over My servants, except the deviant who follow you
phrases.explanation: Satan has no authority over Allah’s servants, except those who choose to follow him and deviate. The verse rejects the idea that temptation removes a person’s responsibility for responding to it.

phrases.translation: and surely Hell is their destined place, all together
phrases.explanation: Hell is the destined place for Satan and those who follow him. The consequence is presented as a collective outcome for people who choose the path of deviation. Their path leads to the outcome they chose.

phrases.translation: It has seven gates, to each a group of them is designated.”
phrases.explanation: Hell has seven gates, with a designated group assigned to each. The verse portrays punishment as ordered and apportioned, not as an uncontrolled or arbitrary event. The allocation reflects the final judgment described.

phrases.translation: Indeed, the righteous will be amid Gardens and springs
phrases.explanation: The righteous will be among Gardens and springs. The image contrasts their place of safety and refreshment with the punishment described immediately before. The Gardens offer relief after the warnings of punishment.

phrases.translation: ˹It will be said to them,˺ “Enter in peace and security.”
phrases.explanation: The righteous are welcomed to enter in peace and security. Their arrival is free from the fear and danger that marked their worldly trials. The greeting assures them their final home is free from harm.

phrases.translation: We will remove whatever bitterness they had in their hearts. In a friendly manner, they will be on thrones, facing one another
phrases.explanation: Allah removes bitterness from their hearts, and they sit together as friends facing one another. Paradise is described as a place of reconciliation and companionship, without lingering resentment. Differences that divided them no longer remain.

phrases.translation: No fatigue will touch them there, nor will they ever be asked to leave
phrases.explanation: No fatigue touches the people of Paradise, and they are never asked to leave. Their comfort is lasting rather than a temporary rest that ends in renewed hardship. Their residence is permanent and secure.

phrases.translation: Inform My servants ˹O Prophet˺ that I am truly the All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is told to inform Allah’s servants that He is All-Forgiving and Most Merciful. The message invites people to hope in forgiveness instead of assuming their past excludes them from mercy.

phrases.translation: and that My torment is indeed the most painful
phrases.explanation: Allah’s torment is also described as intensely painful. The warning balances the invitation to hope with a reminder that persistent wrongdoing has serious consequences. Neither the warning nor the invitation to repent should be ignored.

phrases.translation: And inform them ˹O Prophet˺ about Abraham’s guests
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is told to relate the account of Abraham’s guests. Their visit begins a story about hospitality, unexpected news, and the mission that brings them to Lot’s people. The story moves from hospitality toward the fate of Lot’s people.

phrases.translation: who entered upon him and greeted ˹him with˺, “Peace!” He ˹later˺ said, “Surely we are afraid of you.”
phrases.explanation: The guests greet Abraham with peace, but he later says he is afraid of them. Their arrival is unexpected, and his fear shows that he does not yet understand their purpose.

phrases.translation: They reassured ˹him˺, “Do not be afraid! Surely we give you good news of a knowledgeable son.”
phrases.explanation: The guests tell Abraham not to fear and announce a knowledgeable son. Their reassurance changes the atmosphere of his encounter from uncertainty to the promise of family news. The news is possible by Allah’s command.

phrases.translation: He wondered, “Do you give me good news despite my old age? What unlikely news!”
phrases.explanation: Abraham is astonished to receive the news despite his old age and asks how such a birth is possible. His surprise reflects the improbability of the announcement from a human perspective.

phrases.translation: They responded, “We give you good news in all truth, so do not be one of those who despair.”
phrases.explanation: The messengers affirm that their news is true and tell Abraham not to despair. Their words direct him from the limits of his age toward the possibility of Allah’s mercy.

phrases.translation: He exclaimed, “Who would despair of the mercy of their Lord except the misguided?”
phrases.explanation: Abraham asks who could despair of the mercy of their Lord except the misguided. The question expresses confidence that Allah’s mercy remains open, even when a promise seems unlikely. Abraham trusts divine mercy beyond ordinary expectations.

phrases.translation: He ˹then˺ added, “What is your mission, O messenger-angels?”
phrases.explanation: After hearing the good news, Abraham asks the messenger-angels about their mission. He wants to understand why they have come beyond their announcement about a son. His question shows both hospitality and discernment.

phrases.translation: They replied, “We have actually been sent to a wicked people
phrases.explanation: The angels explain that they have been sent to a wicked people. Their mission is connected with the wrongdoing of Lot’s community, not merely with Abraham’s household. The explanation leads directly to the next stage of their visit.

phrases.translation: As for the family of Lot, we will certainly deliver them all
phrases.explanation: The angels promise to deliver Lot’s family. The assurance distinguishes those to be rescued from the wider community facing judgment. The family will not be treated as one undivided group.

phrases.translation: except his wife. We have determined that she will be one of the doomed.”
phrases.explanation: Lot’s wife is excluded because she is destined to be among the doomed. The verse makes clear that family membership alone does not determine a person’s response or outcome. The narrative distinguishes her from those protected by the promise.

phrases.translation: So when the messengers came to the family of Lot
phrases.explanation: The messengers arrive at Lot’s home. Their visit brings the warning about the people of Lot to the family directly and sets the stage for the events that follow. Their arrival begins the final warning to the city.

phrases.translation: he said, “You are surely an unfamiliar people!”
phrases.explanation: Lot tells the visitors that they are unfamiliar to him. His uncertainty shows that they are strangers, and he does not yet know why they have come. He has not yet learned why they arrived.

phrases.translation: They responded, “We have come to you with that ˹torment˺ which they have doubted
phrases.explanation: The messengers say they have come with the punishment that Lot’s people doubted. The warning is now moving from a disputed claim to an approaching event. The people had dismissed an earlier warning.

phrases.translation: We come to you with the truth, and we are certainly truthful
phrases.explanation: They say they have come with truth and are truthful. Their statement assures Lot that the warning is reliable and that their mission is not based on rumor or deception.

phrases.translation: So travel with your family in the dark of night, and follow ˹closely˺ behind them. Do not let any of you look back, and go where you are commanded.”
phrases.explanation: Lot is told to leave at night with his family, follow behind, avoid looking back, and go where commanded. The careful instructions help the family escape before judgment overtakes the city.

phrases.translation: We revealed to him this decree: “Those ˹sinners˺ will be uprooted in the morning.”
phrases.explanation: Allah reveals that the sinners will be uprooted in the morning. The fixed time explains the urgency of Lot’s departure and makes clear that the warning is near. The fixed time leaves little room to delay.

phrases.translation: And there came the men of the city, rejoicing
phrases.explanation: The men of the city arrive rejoicing. Their excitement reflects their intention toward Lot’s guests, turning the visit into a threat that Lot must confront. Their goal is to reach Lot’s guests.

phrases.translation: Lot pleaded, “Indeed, these are my guests, so do not embarrass me
phrases.explanation: Lot pleads that the visitors are his guests and asks the men not to embarrass him. He appeals to the duty to protect visitors from harm and humiliation. Hospitality here entails active protection.

phrases.translation: Fear Allah and do not humiliate me.”
phrases.explanation: Lot urges the men to fear Allah and not humiliate him. His appeal calls them back to moral restraint and respect for the guests in his care. He appeals to the authority they profess to respect.

phrases.translation: They responded, “Have we not forbidden you from protecting anyone?”
phrases.explanation: The men claim they had forbidden Lot from protecting anyone. Their response shows that they reject his appeal and try to prevent him from defending people under his care. Their refusal leaves Lot isolated.

phrases.translation: He said, “O my people! Here are my daughters ˹so marry them˺ if you wish to do so.”
phrases.explanation: Lot offers his daughters for marriage if the men wish to do so. He directs them toward a lawful relationship rather than allowing them to violate and humiliate his guests.

phrases.translation: By your life ˹O Prophet˺, they certainly wandered blindly, intoxicated ˹by lust˺
phrases.explanation: The verse says the men wandered blindly, overcome by lust. Their desire has displaced judgment and led them to ignore Lot’s appeal and the rights of his guests. The verse condemns their loss of restraint.

phrases.translation: So the ˹mighty˺ blast overtook them at sunrise
phrases.explanation: A mighty blast overtakes the people at sunrise. The timing marks the arrival of the punishment after Lot and his family were told to leave during the night. The city had already received a warning.

phrases.translation: And We turned the cities ˹of Sodom and Gomorrah˺ upside down and rained upon them stones of baked clay
phrases.explanation: The cities are overturned and struck with stones of baked clay. The verse describes a decisive judgment on the people who persisted in wrongdoing. The imagery conveys a complete reversal of the city’s security.

phrases.translation: Surely in this are signs for those who contemplate
phrases.explanation: The event contains signs for people who contemplate. Reflecting on the fate of the cities can warn later communities against repeating the same injustice. Its remains preserve a warning for later generations.

phrases.translation: Their ruins still lie along a known route
phrases.explanation: The ruins remain along a known route. Their visible location makes the history accessible to travelers who pass by and are willing to reflect. The route keeps the historical trace near everyday travel.

phrases.translation: Surely in this is a sign for those who believe
phrases.explanation: The ruins are a sign for those who believe. Faith makes people more ready to recognize the lesson in what happened to earlier communities. Believers take the event as a lesson in accountability.

phrases.translation: And the residents of the Forest were truly wrongdoers
phrases.explanation: The residents of the Forest were also wrongdoers. The verse introduces another community whose conduct placed it among the peoples that faced punishment. The account now turns to another community’s conduct.

phrases.translation: so We inflicted punishment upon them. The ruins of both nations still lie on a well-known road
phrases.explanation: Punishment was inflicted on them, and the ruins of both nations remain along a known road. Their remains provide a visible reminder that wrongdoing can bring lasting consequences. Their ruins preserve a record of the result.

phrases.translation: Indeed, the residents of the Stone Valley also denied the messengers
phrases.explanation: The residents of the Stone Valley deny the messengers, repeating the pattern of earlier peoples. The verse introduces another community that rejects prophetic warning despite the examples before it. The same pattern of denial appears again.

phrases.translation: We gave them Our signs, but they turned away from them
phrases.explanation: The people received clear signs, yet chose to turn away. The verse links their rejection to deliberate response, not lack of evidence. Receiving guidance does not guarantee that a community will accept it.

phrases.translation: They carved their homes in the mountains, feeling secure
phrases.explanation: They carved dwellings into the mountains and treated them as secure. Their impressive homes could not make them invulnerable, a contrast made explicit when punishment arrived the next morning. Shelter alone could not save them.

phrases.translation: But the ˹mighty˺ blast overtook them in the morning
phrases.explanation: The mighty blast overtook them in the morning. Their strength and carved dwellings did not prevent the punishment, continuing the account’s warning that human security cannot overcome Allah’s decree. No fortress could help.

phrases.translation: and all they achieved was of no help to them
phrases.explanation: Everything they had built, earned, or relied upon failed to help them. The verse closes the account of the people of the Stone Valley by contrasting their achievements with their inability to avert judgment.

phrases.translation: We have not created the heavens and the earth and everything in between except for a purpose. And the Hour is certain to come, so forgive graciously
phrases.explanation: The heavens, earth, and all between them are created with purpose, not without meaning. Since the Hour will certainly come, the Prophet is told to forgive graciously, answering opposition with dignity while trusting ultimate justice to Allah.

phrases.translation: Surely your Lord is the Master Creator, All-Knowing
phrases.explanation: Allah is described as the Creator who knows all. This assurance connects purposeful creation and the coming Hour to the One who made the world and fully knows every person’s actions.

phrases.translation: We have certainly granted you the seven often-repeated verses and the great Quran
phrases.explanation: The seven oft-repeated verses are commonly understood as Surah Al-Fatiha, recited repeatedly in prayer. This verse pairs that gift with the great Quran, honoring both the opening chapter and the wider revelation given to the Prophet.

phrases.translation: Do not let your eyes crave the ˹fleeting˺ pleasures We have provided for some of the disbelievers, nor grieve for them. And be gracious to the believers
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is told not to covet the temporary comforts given to some who disbelieve or be consumed by grief for them. Instead, he is to show graciousness to believers, redirecting attention from status to faithful community.

phrases.translation: And say, “I am truly sent with a clear warning”—
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is instructed to announce that he has been sent as a clear warner. The dash-like ending in the translation leads into the following verses, which clarify the warning by comparing it with earlier revelation.

phrases.translation: ˹a warning˺ similar to what We sent to those who divided ˹the Scriptures˺
phrases.explanation: The warning is compared with what was sent to those who divided the Scriptures. This allusion connects the present message with past communities and cautions against treating revelation as a matter to fragment or manipulate.

phrases.translation: who ˹now˺ accept parts of the Quran, rejecting others
phrases.explanation: The verse describes people who accept some portions of the Quran while rejecting others. Together with the previous verse, it condemns selective handling of revelation when parts are welcomed and other parts resisted.

phrases.translation: So by your Lord! We will certainly question them all
phrases.explanation: An oath by the Lord stresses that all people will be questioned. Accountability is universal, so no one can evade scrutiny by status, denial, selective acceptance, or mockery of the message.

phrases.translation: about what they used to do
phrases.explanation: The coming question concerns actual conduct, not simply a person’s words or group identity. This line completes the warning in the previous verse: each person is accountable for what they practiced.

phrases.translation: So proclaim what you have been commanded, and turn away from the polytheists
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is commanded to proclaim openly what he has been given and turn away from the polytheists. The instruction calls for faithful public witness without letting opposition displace his mission.

phrases.translation: Surely We will be sufficient for you against the mockers
phrases.explanation: Allah promises to be sufficient against those who mock the Prophet and his message. The assurance follows the command to proclaim, strengthening him to continue despite ridicule rather than being defined by it.

phrases.translation: who set up ˹other˺ gods with Allah. They will soon come to know
phrases.explanation: The mockers are identified as people who set up other gods alongside Allah, and they will soon learn the outcome. Their opposition is not merely personal. It is tied to the rejection of worshipping Allah alone.

phrases.translation: We certainly know that your heart is truly distressed by what they say
phrases.explanation: Allah knows the Prophet’s distress at the words of his opponents. Acknowledging that pain offers reassurance: the mockery is not unnoticed, and the Prophet is not left alone to bear it.

phrases.translation: So glorify the praises of your Lord and be one of those who ˹always˺ pray
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is directed to glorify Allah with praise and join those who pray. Worship becomes a response to distress, grounding him in remembrance rather than allowing hostile words to dominate his attention.

phrases.translation: and worship your Lord until the inevitable comes your way
phrases.explanation: Worship is to continue until the inevitable comes, traditionally understood here as death. The closing verse frames devotion as a lifelong commitment, maintained through changing circumstances until a person’s time in this world ends.
